recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It restores the approved clarification on the active CarePlan/ServiceRequest surface without reviving retired DiagnosticRequest wording or changing the ServiceRequest resource model.
issue_request: FHIR-11340 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for DSTU2 DiagnosticRequest. It asked that CarePlan typically reference DiagnosticRequest with a stage of plan or proposal, with those requests sometimes requiring separate initiation and authorization outside the CarePlan.
initial_application: The request was initially applied by git commit ccaebaf26211addd4753b390f79e43735583f08a to source/diagnosticrequest/diagnosticrequest-introduction.xml. Later FHIR-11119 work merged DiagnosticRequest into ProcedureRequest, and a subsequent ProcedureRequest boundaries rewrite removed the DiagnosticRequest-specific CarePlan paragraph.
additional_context: DiagnosticRequest is now a removed resource, while CarePlan and ServiceRequest are active current resources. Current ServiceRequest already represents diagnostic and other service requests as orders, proposals, or plans through ServiceRequest.intent. The active CarePlan boundaries text still used stale status-of-planned wording, which did not match the current request pattern or fully preserve the FHIR-11340 clarification. Community searches found no relevant non-bot Zulip or Confluence evidence that changed the Jira/source-history conclusion.
reconciliation: Updated source/careplan/careplan-introduction.xml to say CarePlan activity references can point to request resources with intent proposal or plan, where independent initiation or authorization may still be required, or to resources that already represent active orders.
source_changes: source/careplan/careplan-introduction.xml: replaced stale request-resource "status" of planned wording with current request intent proposal/plan wording and added the independent initiation/authorization nuance.

related_jiras.note: Published issue that combined DiagnosticRequest and ProcedureRequest, explaining why the original FHIR-11340 source page is no longer current.
Later request-resource boundary/merge work that led toward the current ServiceRequest surface carrying these diagnostic request semantics.
